scenes.title: Create a traceable record
scenes.narration: An experiment evidence log connects a claim, planned method, actual records and interpretation. Label planned, not run, rehearsal or actual status. A completed lesson is not an experiment conducted.

scenes.title: Preserve the original design
scenes.narration: Bring your value proposition claim, format, measurement definitions and commitment assumptions together. Preserve the original evidence rule. Review earlier drafts manually; the prototype imports no data automatically.

scenes.title: Record execution and deviations
scenes.narration: For an actual test, record what happened and any changes, assistance, interruptions or deviations. Do not rewrite the original plan to fit a result. If no test ran, write not conducted and keep result fields unknown.

scenes.title: Index sources and counts
scenes.visual: Anonymous source codes and outcome categories
scenes.narration: Link records to anonymous source codes and authorised secure references. Keep duplicates, missingness, denominator, assistance and cancellations visible. Do not upload private source records into this worksheet.

scenes.title: Interpret within the rule
scenes.narration: Compare the bounded result with the original rule and state alternative explanations. Preserve contradictions. A prototype action or time commitment does not automatically prove adoption, payment, retention or a market-wide rate.

scenes.title: Close the learning pack
scenes.narration: Create your Experiment Evidence Log and choose the next review action. All five lessons must be completed separately to close Module 2.3. Learning completion does not verify source accuracy, approve launch or validate demand.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Make the path from plan to conclusion visible.

children: An
evidence log
connects the original claim and review rule to records and interpretation. A
deviation
is a change from the planned method.
Traceability
lets a reviewer follow a conclusion back to its sources.
Assign an experiment code and honest status.
Preserve the original claim, method and before-test review rule.
Record execution and deviations, or explicitly mark not conducted.
Index anonymous sources, quality, missingness and bounded counts.
Compare results to the original rule; keep inference separate.
State limits and a next learning action with an owner.
Planned / not run
Design and evidence template can be complete while execution and results remain “not conducted / unknown.” Do not enter measured zeros or invent participants.
Rehearsal / actual
Fictional rehearsal is practice, not customer evidence. Actual records need honest source references and context; completion cannot verify them.
Illustrative planned log

E01: not run. Claim: a relevant adult can explain a registration concept without coaching. Format: labeled concept card. Original rule: an uncoached accurate explanation supports clarity only; coaching or unclear source data is inconclusive. Execution: not conducted, access pending. Sources/results: none/unknown. Next action: resolve access and safeguards before a permitted check. No adoption or payment claim.

If a facilitator helped during an actual check, record it as a deviation; do not quietly count an assisted outcome as unassisted. Keep rejected assumptions, cancelled sessions and contrary records visible. Do not change the original rule after seeing results without recording the change and its effect.

Review Lessons 31–34 manually; they save separately and are not auto-imported. Use anonymous summaries here, with private originals in an approved secure system. No upload, analytics, source verification, transaction handling or experiment execution is connected.
